finding.title: Fix the awk field-split bug in `make audit` check 15/15 that makes cross-feature-import detection a permanent no-op

evidence.quote: match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print

finding.why: Check 15/15's awk splits each `grep -rn` hit on ':' and calls match($1,...) for the file's own feature and match($0,...) for the import's feature, expecting them to differ on a real violation. But $0 is the whole line, and `grep -rn` always prints `path:line:content` first — since the file path itself contains 'features/<name>/', match($0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//) finds that occurrence (the file's OWN feature) before ever reaching the import text, so a[1] and b[1] are always equal and `if(a[1] != b[1])` never fires. Reproduced by hand: piping step_chazara.dart's onboarding import through the exact command yields a1=tracks b1=tracks. The captured baseline (docs/audits/standards-audit-2026-07-03/_work/baseline/make-audit.txt) confirms this: check 14/15 (core→features, different/working logic) lists 32 edges, check 15/15 prints nothing at all. A hand grep across just this 30-file batch turns up 25 real cross-feature deep imports across 13 files (onboarding, scheduler, settings, content_browsing, profiles, sync, progress, dashboard) — none of which the 'audit PASSED' result reflects.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk to derive the file's own feature from a fixed prefix match on $1 only, and the import's feature from the substring AFTER the 'package:learning_tracker/features/' marker in the import text specifically (not the first 'features/' in the whole line) — e.g. split on the import URI, not on ':'. Then run it for real, triage the resulting list the same way the 32 known core→features edges were baselined, and decide per-edge whether to introduce features/<Y>/providers.dart barrels or accept/document the exception.
acceptance_criteria: `make audit` check 15/15, run against the current tree, prints at least the 25 known violations found in this batch (not zero).
A regression fixture (a deliberately-added cross-feature deep import in a scratch file) causes check 15/15 to fail non-zero, then passes again once removed.
The resulting violation list is triaged/baselined the same way check 14/15's 32 edges are, in the same PR.
